delivery_checks: Native Note copy written for the Notes feed, not a pasted article excerpt; every quote is a literal match to the published piece.

Any image: made in a Claude session, with the Codex plugin building it (Ruling, Krish, 2026-11-13; content-engine docs/CAROUSEL-STANDARD.md, "How a carousel is made"): the session writes the words and the direction, a Codex card of kind notes_image builds the picture in code, and the session verifies it against the brand palette before Krish sees it; never a scheduled job, a headless model run or a template engine. It is filed in its post's 3 Posts folder.
No outside link in a reach Note; verify the subscribe path live.

Share mechanic: one line a reader would quote or forward to a named person, complete without the article behind it. It stays a proposal in the brief until content-engine adopts it as a production standard through its own route.
Before Krish sees it: a complete share block (social/share.json), no generic share call to action in the copy, and a blind send test whose reader names the declared receiver and job (crew/send-test).
Bind publication approval to the exact account, caption, ordered asset hashes, metadata and proposed time.
After a save, wait and independently reopen; reconcile uncertain outcomes before retrying.
measurements: Primary measure (Krish, 28 October 2026): sends, meaning native shares, per reach and saves per reach against the format's own channel median; a house hypothesis until MYMU's own dated data confirms it (lesson share-rate-measure).
Dated exposed reach and meaningful engagement, preserving missing values.
Relevant follower/profile movement and source-attributed publication subscriptions where exposed.
24-hour, 72-hour and seven-day readback after actual publication; no financial ROI inference from draft counts.
Note clicks, restacks and free subscribers attributed to Notes where Substack or Buffer exposes them.
